title: Muslim neighbors
hookLine: the Church esteems Muslims who worship the one God (Nostra Aetate 3)

lines: A MAT IN THE SUPPLY ROOM.
A ROSARY IN A SCRUB POCKET.
cards: Five in the afternoon at a hospital nurses' station. One nurse steps into a supply room, unrolls a small mat, and turns toward the direction she worked out in her first week.
Another nurse, a Catholic with a rosary in her scrub pocket, covers the call lights until she's back. Nobody makes a speech. They just know each other's rhythms.
A document from the Second Vatican Council, Nostra Aetate, has a short paragraph about exactly this kind of neighbor. Today, Muslim neighbors.

teach.h: THE CHURCH REGARDS MUSLIMS WITH ESTEEM.
teach.b: Back on day three hundred twenty-one, this paragraph got a single line. Today, the whole of it. It opens with one word that sets the tone: esteem.
The Church regards Muslims with esteem, real regard, more than tolerance or politeness. Then it says why, naming what Muslims actually believe and do, in terms Muslims would recognize.
They worship the one God, living, merciful and all-powerful, Creator of heaven and earth, who has spoken to humankind.
They strive to submit wholeheartedly to God's decrees, as Abraham did, and Islam gladly links its faith to Abraham.

teach.h: JESUS REVERED AS PROPHET; MARY HONORED.
teach.b: Muslims do not acknowledge Jesus as God, the text says, but they revere him as a prophet. They honor Mary, his virgin mother, and at times call on her with devotion.
The council states the difference about Jesus plainly, and still chooses esteem. Muslims await a day of judgment and the raising of the dead.

teach.h: PRAYER, ALMS, FASTING, AND A SHARED TASK.
teach.b: They value the moral life, and worship God especially through prayer, almsgiving and fasting; Catholics keep those same practices in Lent. Finally the council looks back honestly.

It admits quarrels and hostilities between Christians and Muslims, and asks both to move past them, to work sincerely for mutual understanding, and together to protect social justice, moral welfare, peace and freedom for everyone.
Esteem, then what's shared, then what differs, then a job to do together. It's a short text, and it fits at a nurses' station.

how: Catholic teaching on Muslims draws on the Second Vatican Council's declaration Nostra Aetate, which speaks of esteem. Some parishes and dioceses hold meetings, shared meals or service projects with local mosques.

games.why: it asks Christians and Muslims to move past old hostilities and work together for social justice, moral welfare, peace and freedom.

practice: Let one Muslim you actually know, or see often, come to mind: a coworker, a classmate, the family two doors down, the man who runs the corner shop.
Recall one thing you know about their day, when they pray or what they care about, hold them with esteem for a moment, and choose a simple greeting for next time; hello, and their name, is plenty.
If you pray, you can hold them before God.

wordCard.voice: Muslim neighbors. In Nostra Aetate the Church regards them with esteem, as worshipers of the one God who pray, give alms and fast. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: peace be upon you. the reply wa alaykum as-salam means and upon you be peace.

carryVoice: Your line: with esteem. Shared ground and real difference, held side by side. See you tomorrow.
